categories.label: Logic / state
categories.description: incorrect control flow, business logic or state transitions

categories.label: Boundary / arithmetic
categories.description: off-by-one errors, numeric overflow or wrong boundary handling

categories.label: Resource lifecycle
categories.description: resource leaks or incorrect allocation, cleanup or lifetime management

categories.label: Concurrency
categories.description: races, deadlocks or incorrect synchronization

categories.label: Error handling
categories.description: incorrect exception handling, missing error checks or recovery behavior

categories.label: Compatibility
categories.description: broken platform, version, protocol or integration compatibility

categories.label: Data integrity
categories.description: incorrect serialization, persistence, parsing or data transformation

categories.label: Performance bug fix
categories.description: pathological runtime, excessive work or unintended performance regressions

categories.label: UI / accessibility
categories.description: incorrect user-interface behavior or inaccessible interaction

categories.label: Other bug
categories.description: a behavioral bug that is not covered by logic/state, boundary/arithmetic, resource lifecycle, concurrency, error handling, compatibility, data integrity, performance, or UI/accessibility

categories.label: Cross-site scripting
categories.description: untrusted content reaching an executable browser HTML or script context without appropriate neutralization

categories.label: SQL injection
categories.description: untrusted input changing the structure of an SQL command

categories.label: OS command injection
categories.description: untrusted input changing an operating-system command

categories.label: Path traversal
categories.description: untrusted paths escaping the intended restricted directory

categories.label: Improper authentication
categories.description: failure to correctly verify an actor’s claimed identity

categories.label: Missing authorization
categories.description: an absent permission check before access to a protected resource or action

categories.label: Information exposure
categories.description: sensitive information exposed to an unauthorized actor

categories.label: Use after free
categories.description: access to memory after its allocation has been freed

categories.label: Out-of-bounds write
categories.description: writing outside the bounds of an allocated memory buffer

categories.label: Out-of-bounds read
categories.description: reading outside the bounds of an allocated memory buffer

categories.label: Race condition
categories.description: a security-relevant race in concurrent access to shared state without proper synchronization

categories.label: Resource exhaustion
categories.description: uncontrolled resource consumption allowing denial of service

categories.label: Server-side request forgery
categories.description: an attacker influencing a server to send unintended requests to other resources

categories.label: Cross-site request forgery
categories.description: a site accepting an attacker-induced authenticated request without checking the user’s intent

categories.label: Unsafe deserialization
categories.description: deserialization of untrusted data with unsafe object or code effects

categories.label: Broken cryptography
categories.description: use of a cryptographic algorithm that is broken or too risky for the security purpose

categories.label: Other security weakness
categories.description: a security weakness outside XSS, SQL/OS command injection, path traversal, authentication, missing authorization, information exposure, memory bounds/lifetime, races, resource exhaustion, SSRF, CSRF, unsafe deserialization, and broken cryptographic algorithms

categories.label: Performance improvement
categories.description: reduce latency, runtime work, memory use or I/O, or improve throughput or scalability; an existing defect is not required

categories.label: New feature
categories.description: add or extend an externally usable capability or behavior

categories.label: Refactoring
categories.description: restructure implementation while preserving intended externally observable behavior

categories.label: Security hardening
categories.description: strengthen security controls or defense in depth, even without evidence of a specific pre-existing vulnerability

categories.label: Dependency
categories.description: add, remove, upgrade, downgrade, pin or otherwise update a dependency, including version or resolution changes in manifests and lockfiles, or adapt source code to a changed library, dependency, framework or runtime API

categories.label: Observability
categories.description: add or improve diagnostic logging, metrics, tracing, profiling or operational visibility

categories.label: Compatibility expansion
categories.description: add support for a platform, protocol, format or version, without requiring previously broken support

categories.label: Build / deployment
categories.description: change executable build, packaging, deployment or release automation

categories.label: Reliability improvement
categories.description: improve recovery, retries, fault tolerance or graceful degradation, without requiring a demonstrated prior defect

categories.label: Code cleanup
categories.description: remove dead or redundant code or improve names, organization or maintainability

categories.label: API / schema change
categories.description: change a public interface, data contract, persistent schema or wire format

categories.label: UX / accessibility improvement
categories.description: improve user interaction, presentation, usability or accessibility without requiring a demonstrated prior defect

coreQuestions.bug_fix: Does the actual code change correct a pre-existing defect in behavior? Feature additions, pure refactoring, documentation-only edits and a claimed fix in the message without code evidence are not sufficient.
coreQuestions.security_fix: Does the actual code change mitigate a pre-existing security weakness that could affect confidentiality, integrity or availability? Do not infer security impact merely because a normal bug was fixed or the message claims security.
coreQuestions.behavior_change: Does this change alter executable behavior, rather than only formatting, comments, documentation or equivalent refactoring?
coreQuestions.insufficient_context: Is the supplied evidence insufficient to reliably determine whether this change fixes a pre-existing bug or security weakness?
